title: Chi-square law for multidimensional linear capacity
summary: Prove the conjectured chi-square distribution and degree of freedom for multidimensional linear approximations of a random permutation.

formal_statement.body: Let $F$ be uniformly random among permutations of $\mathbb F_2^n$. For every source-admissible $t$-dimensional linear approximation $\Lambda$ whose trivial input- and output-mask subspaces have dimensions $u$ and $v$, respectively, prove or refute $$2^n\operatorname{Cap}(\Lambda)\sim\chi^2_{2^t-2^u-2^v+1}.$$ A refutation must give an admissible approximation family with a different distribution or degree of freedom.

scope.domain: Multidimensional linear approximations of uniformly random binary permutations
assumptions: F is uniformly random over all permutations of F_2^n
Lambda is a source-admissible t-dimensional linear approximation
The trivial input and output mask subspaces have dimensions u and v
scope.unresolved_remainder: The Davies--Meyer special case is proved in the source, but the exact distribution for general random permutations remains conjectural.

progress.summary: The source conjectures the general random-permutation law after proving the Davies--Meyer special case.
